text:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — I sketched a lightweight "rate-guesser" service to tag incoming requests with a cost class before admission. Goal: improve fairness decisions without waiting for full tokenization. Thoughts?
arpan: Love the name. How is this different from the current token-count heuristic we already do in ingress?
maya: Current heuristic runs after we unwrap payload and is expensive for long prompts. Guesser uses shallow stats + a tiny model that runs in the frontdoor (<1ms), gives classes like interactive|batch|embed|replay and an estimated token-range.
jun: We can't forward raw prompts to a classifier because of PII. What inputs does it need?
maya: Only headers + content-length + model name + a couple redacted signal tokens (first N/last N hashed). No raw text leaves the frontdoor unless customer opts in.
sam: What's the enforcement contract? If guesser says "batch" but actual tokens are high, do we penalize the client?
maya: Plan is: enforcement uses guessed class for admission shaping only. Final accounting uses real token counts returned asynchronously. If misclassification rate high we adjust weights or fall back to conservative shaping for that client.
leah: Also need to think about adaptive attackers who purposefully craft payloads to look low-cost. Can we combine with abuse signals?
maya: Yup — abuse score + guesser class => admission score. If mismatch between guessed and actual exceeds threshold, bump client's suspicion and route to stricter lanes.
arpan: Interface wise, do we want a separate RPC (frontdoor -> rate-guesser) or embed as a local library to avoid extra RPC latency?
maya: Prototype as a sidecar RPC so we can iterate quickly. Long term we can A/B embedding into frontdoor runtime for perf-critical paths.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rate-guesser v0.1 to staging cluster scheduled at 20:00 UTC :rocket:
jun: Telemetry is key. Need a per-request correlation id and histogram of guess vs actual token counts. We should export a confusion matrix daily.
maya: Agreed — telemetry events: guessed_class, guessed_range, actual_tokens, model, client_id, final_action.
sam: How do we handle streaming / chunked requests where tokens accumulate over time?
maya: For streaming, guess on first chunk and allow periodic reclassification at chunk boundaries. Admission uses the latest known class but we keep a fast-path to escalate if runtime token growth exceeds guess.
leah: Rollout plan idea: dark-lift (log guesses, no impact) -> compare distribution to real counts -> opt-in 10% -> gradual 100% with rollback window. Also run targeted tests on high-volume tenants.
arpan: Security: accept guesser headers only from our trusted frontdoor. If third-party proxies inject headers we ignore unless signed. Avoid trusting client-supplied X-Rate-Class.
maya: Example header we propose:
```
X-Redwood-Rate-Class: interactive
X-Redwood-Rate-Estimate: 0-128
X-Redwood-Rate-Guess-Sig: v1:abcd...  # frontdoor signs it
```
sam: Nice. One more product tradeoff: per-class fairness slices vs dynamic soft-shaping. Hard slices are simpler but can underutilize capacity.
leah: Agreed. Suggest we start with soft-shaping (weights) by class and monitor utilization. If an abuse vector emerges, we can hard-isolate slices for specific tenants.
jun: For observability, add a dashboard showing misclassification latency, false-neg rates by model & tenant, and cost delta if we used guessed vs actual earlier.
maya: Next steps: I'll push a proto and a staging sidecar image. Can folks review the proto when I post it? I'll also add the rollout checklist for dark-lift.
arpan: Review when posted. Also include an experiment plan for simulated adversarial payloads.
ops-bot: reminder: weekly infra sync Fri 15:00 — add a short demo to agenda :calendar:
maya: Thanks — posting proto in #eng-platform and opening a tiny RFC doc in the repo tonight. :thumbsup:
